claim_being_audited: The actor claims the model can be certified for rollout because aggregate readiness passed and rollout controls exist, provided the known food safety inspection limitation is contemporaneously disclosed or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
decision_criteria: If the affected use case was excluded from rollout, certification would be more supportable under the stated policy.
If approved risk acceptance specifically covering the exposed segment existed before launch, certification would be more supportable under the stated policy.
If contemporaneous disclosure of the known limitation in the model card is proven, the actor's constrained certification theory becomes materially stronger.
Absent exclusion, approved risk acceptance, or proven disclosure, certification remains insufficiently supported under the stated policy.
evidence_requests: Provide the final model card or disclosure record showing the food safety inspection limitation was explicitly disclosed before launch.
Provide approved risk acceptance, if any, specifically addressing continued food safety inspection exposure.
Provide rollout cohort evidence showing whether the affected use case was excluded or remained included at launch.
Provide the underlying contents of the cited evidence items, not just their IDs or summary characterizations.
specific_concerns: The affected food safety inspection segment is described as still exposed and below target.
The policy text says rollout controls do not remove disclosure duties when the affected segment remains exposed.
No admissible evidence is provided here that the affected use case is excluded from rollout.
No admissible evidence is provided here that reviewed risk acceptance was approved before launch.
No admissible evidence is provided here that the required model-card disclosure was actually completed before certification.
unsupported_claims: That certification is presently compliant as a locked decision, rather than only conditionally supportable, without direct evidence of completed disclosure, exclusion, or approved risk acceptance.
That public governance guidance meaningfully cures the policy gap; the controlling policy text governs and the cited public guidance is not necessary to establish compliance.
Any implication that limited rollout percentage, rollback capability, or monitoring alone make the certification compliant while the exposed segment remains in scope.
